'''''Linguistics and Philosophy''''' is a peer-reviewed journal which publishes work addressing [[meaning (linguistics)|meaning]] and structure in [[natural language]].<ref name="L&P">{{Cite web|title=Linguistics and Philosophy|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10988|access-date=2024-08-31|website=Springer|language=en}}</ref> It is one of four top journals in formal semantics, alongside [[Natural Language Semantics]], the [[Journal of Semantics]], and [[Semantics and Pragmatics]].<ref name="StanfordEncyclopediaOfPhilosophy">{{Citation|last1=Janssen|first1=Theo|last2=Zimmermann|first2=Ede|title=Montague semantics|date=2021|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/montague-semantics/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Summer 2021|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2024-08-07|quote=The most important journals in the field are Linguistics and Philosophy, the Journal of Semantics, Natural Language Semantics, and Semantics and Pragmatics}}</ref> Papers in the journal tend to emphasize concerns shared by linguists and philosophers, and are intended to be accessible to readers from both fields.<ref name="parteebaltic">{{cite journal |last1=Partee|first1=Barbara|author-link=Barbara Partee|year=2011|title= Formal semantics: Origins, issues, early impact.|journal=The Baltic International Yearbook of Cognition, Logic and Communication|volume=6|citeseerx=10.1.1.826.5720}}</ref>

The journal is a continuation of the earlier '''''Foundations of Language''''' which had been founded by [[Frits Staal]] in order to encourage interaction between linguists, philosophers, and logicians.<ref>{{cite conference|title=The Intertwining Influences of Logic, Philosophy, and Linguistics in the Development of Formal Semantics and Pragmatics|last=Partee|first=Barbara |author-link=Barbara Partee|year=2018|pages=9,47|location=Amsterdam}}</ref> The current Editors-in-Chief are philosopher [[Michael Glanzberg]] ([[Rutgers University]]) and linguist [[Yael Sharvit]] ([[UCLA]]).<ref name="L&P"/>
